verdict.rationale: First-party testing docs describe two layers. A `tests/` suite of bash, node and python integration tests covers the plugin's non-LLM code. An `evals/` Python harness drives real tmux sessions of Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance. The writing-skills skill also requires skills to be built test-first against pressure scenarios. Community 'it's all vibes' skepticism is general, not a concrete counter-example, so it lowers confidence only. Missing for 10: evidence that evals run automatically on every change or gate releases (CI regression runs), and independent or hands-on corroboration that the eval harness works as described.
